texto_en: The indicator is NEET: not being employed and not participating in education or training. Cite the age range 15–29 years.
The indicator combines employment and participation in education; it does not describe each of those two dimensions separately.
Eurostat · Disability statistics – access to education and training
Persons aged 25 to 34, with and without disabilities
of young persons with disabilities had a high level of education.
The figure compares the educational level attained by persons aged 25 to 34 with and without disabilities. It does not measure current university enrolment or dropout from a specific degree.
The indicator describes a high level of education in the population aged 25–34. It does not measure university access among current students.
The indicator refers to a specific age group and to educational level attained.
Eurostat · Disability statistics – access to education and training
Adults aged 25 to 64, previous four weeks
of those with a severe disability had participated in education or training during the previous four weeks.
The statistic measures participation by adults aged 25 to 64 in education or training during the previous four weeks. It is an indicator of lifelong learning, not of accumulated formal education.
Participation refers to education or training during the previous four weeks among persons aged 25–64.
The reference period is short: participation during the previous four weeks.

In the EU, persons with disabilities are more exposed to poverty and social exclusion. In 2024, 28.8% were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, compared with 17.9% of persons without activity limitation.
